faq.q: What is a Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP)?
faq.a: A DRHP is a preliminary document filed with SEBI by a company planning an IPO. It contains detailed information about the company's business, financials, promoters, risks, and the proposed IPO structure, but without the final price or number of shares.

faq.q: How can I apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your demat and trading account provider (broker) using the ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility. Your bank account funds will be blocked until allotment, without being debited.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment for an IPO?
faq.a: The minimum investment in an IPO is typically for one 'lot' of shares, which is a fixed number of shares. The total value of one lot usually ranges from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000.

faq.q: Is investing in an IPO always profitable?
faq.a: No, investing in an IPO is not always profitable. While some IPOs see significant listing gains, others may list at a discount or perform poorly post-listing due to market conditions or company-specific issues.

faq.q: How do I know if an IPO is oversubscribed?
faq.a: During the IPO subscription period, most brokerage platforms and financial news websites provide live updates on the subscription status in different investor categories (retail, HNI, QIB).

faq.q: What happens if an IPO is cancelled?
faq.a: If an IPO is cancelled, any funds blocked under the ASBA facility for your application will be unblocked and become available in your bank account.

faq.q: Where can I find official IPO documents?
faq.a: All official IPO documents, including the DRHP and RHP, are available on the SEBI website (sebi.gov.in) under the 'Filings' section, as well as on the websites of the lead managers to the issue.
